concepts.name: Parts of speech
concepts.summary: Recognise and name nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, pronouns, prepositions and conjunctions and say what job each does.

concepts.name: Subject and predicate
concepts.summary: Explain that a basic sentence has a subject that names who or what and a predicate that says what it does or is.

concepts.name: Complete sentences
concepts.summary: Tell a complete sentence from a fragment by checking for a subject, a finite verb and a complete thought.

concepts.name: Singular and plural nouns
concepts.summary: Form regular and common irregular plurals and understand that number changes the noun's form.

concepts.name: Basic verb tenses
concepts.summary: Understand how simple present, past and future tenses place an action in time.

concepts.name: Capitalisation and end punctuation
aliases: capital letters, full stops, question marks
concepts.summary: Remember to capitalise sentence starts and proper nouns and to end sentences with a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark.

concepts.name: Subject pronouns and object pronouns
concepts.summary: Understand that pronouns change form depending on whether they act as subject or object.

misconceptions.text: A sentence is complete whenever it starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.
Every word ending in -s is a plural noun.
A verb is always a word that shows physical action.

concepts.name: Subject-verb agreement
concepts.summary: Make the verb match its subject in number, including with simple compound subjects and words placed between subject and verb.

concepts.name: Apostrophes for possession and contraction
concepts.summary: Apply apostrophes correctly to form possessives and contractions and avoid using them in plurals.

concepts.name: Coordinating and subordinating conjunctions
concepts.summary: Combine simple sentences into compound and complex ones using suitable conjunctions.

concepts.name: Commas in lists and clauses
concepts.summary: Use commas in series, after introductory elements and before coordinating conjunctions joining independent clauses.

concepts.name: Irregular verb forms
concepts.summary: Use the correct past tense and past participle of common irregular verbs.

concepts.name: Perfect and progressive tenses
concepts.summary: Choose and form perfect and progressive tenses to show completed, ongoing or repeated actions.

concepts.name: Adjective and adverb forms
concepts.summary: Choose between adjective and adverb and form comparatives and superlatives correctly.

misconceptions.text: Use an apostrophe whenever a noun is made plural.
A comma can join two independent clauses on its own.
Put a comma wherever you would pause when speaking.

concepts.name: Independent and dependent clauses
concepts.summary: Analyse sentences to identify clause types and how they build simple, compound, complex and compound-complex sentences.

concepts.name: Run-ons and comma splices
concepts.summary: Diagnose run-ons and comma splices and repair them with punctuation, conjunctions or restructuring.

concepts.name: Relative clauses and restrictiveness
concepts.summary: Use relative pronouns and punctuate restrictive and non-restrictive clauses correctly.

concepts.name: Pronoun reference and case
concepts.summary: Analyse pronoun antecedents for clarity and agreement and select correct case, including who and whom.

concepts.name: Parallel structure
concepts.summary: Spot and correct faulty parallelism in lists, comparisons and paired constructions.

concepts.name: Modifier placement
concepts.summary: Identify misplaced and dangling modifiers and revise so the modifier attaches to the intended word.

concepts.name: Semicolons, colons and dashes
concepts.summary: Apply semicolons, colons and dashes according to the grammatical structure they connect.

concepts.name: Active and passive voice
concepts.summary: Analyse when active or passive voice fits the purpose and convert between them.

misconceptions.text: Which and that are always interchangeable in relative clauses.
Whom is just a more formal version of who and can be used anywhere.
The passive voice is always wrong and should be avoided.

concepts.name: Mood and subjunctive
concepts.summary: Analyse how verb mood expresses fact, command or hypothetical and use the subjunctive where standard usage requires it.

concepts.name: Nonfinite verb phrases
concepts.summary: Distinguish infinitives, gerunds and participial phrases and judge their correct use, such as with possessives and verb patterns.

concepts.name: Formal and informal register
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether a grammatical form or usage choice suits an audience, medium and purpose.

concepts.name: Contested usage rules
concepts.summary: Evaluate rules such as split infinitives, stranded prepositions and singular they against evidence of actual usage and authority.

concepts.name: Concord with collective and notional subjects
concepts.summary: Resolve agreement with collective nouns, quantifiers, either/or and notional plurals by analysing meaning and form.

concepts.name: Information structure and emphasis
concepts.summary: Judge how word order, clefting and sentence position affect emphasis and clarity.

concepts.name: Variety of English
concepts.summary: Distinguish major differences in grammar, spelling and punctuation between English varieties and keep a consistent choice.

misconceptions.text: Grammar rules are fixed laws, so any usage that breaks a textbook rule is an error.
The subjunctive has disappeared and never applies in modern English.
Formal writing is always more correct than informal writing.

concepts.name: Editing for style and grammar
concepts.summary: Evaluate a text for grammar, usage and clarity and decide which edits improve it without altering the author's voice.

concepts.name: Applying style guides
concepts.summary: Judge between style guides and apply or reconcile their rulings on punctuation and usage for a given publication.

concepts.name: Diagnosing learner errors
concepts.summary: Evaluate patterns of error to find underlying causes and design targeted explanations or exercises.

concepts.name: Crafting stylistic effect
concepts.summary: Create sentences that use syntax, fragments or rule-bending deliberately for rhythm, tone or rhetorical effect.

concepts.name: Language change and corpus evidence
concepts.summary: Evaluate disputed usage using corpus data and the history of how forms change.

concepts.name: Grammar rule design
concepts.summary: Create clear, evidence-based usage guidance and rules for a defined audience, with justified exceptions.

misconceptions.text: A single authoritative style guide settles every grammar and usage question.
Skilled writers never break grammar rules.
Editing means correcting every deviation from the rules, whatever the context.
